strategy.summary: Blankstahl Werdenfels is a sound, family-owned bar-stock mill-service supplier. It supplies three bars under framework ctr:4600070740, which carries a PPI-C2431 index clause, and it has quoted a fourth part. We are a small customer to it, and its sales director has said three times that it is reviewing small accounts. The index clause has already passed the PPI rise into our prices, and the index has eased since. On the two dual-sourced parts it sits clearly above the parallel sources (370010 vs Donautal, 370012 vs Rupprecht-Kessel). Its quote for sheet 370020 is uncompetitive. 370011 is single-sourced and has the worst lateness, so it is our exposure. Quality is excellent; on-time delivery is weak against the contractual target. The owner has offered an open-book calculation. Price moves above a threshold need its pricing committee, which meets fortnightly. Its open ask is an AS-14404 clause for 370010. The renewal notice window is still open.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner, who is personally engaged and has offered an open calculation, for strategic or price-basis questions. A pricing committee meeting fortnightly approves larger price changes. The key account manager handles day-to-day settlements within his limit; the sales director drives account prioritisation. A newer inside-sales contact handles routine matters.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for any of the four parts, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured. The analysis rests only on index movements, price history and rival prices, so the evidence is thin on cost.

On 2026-07-01 the contract index clause (#3.2) raised prices by about 11% on all three bars: 370010 from 5.26 to 5.84, 370011 from 2.88 to 3.20, and 370012 from 129.13 to 143.39. This matches the formula: 0.8 x the PPI-C2431 rise of about 12.6% from the base gives roughly +10 to +11%. The 12-month PPI-C2431 rise is therefore already priced in, and the index has since fallen 2.3% from its 2026-06 peak. The next quarterly adjustment would only trigger above 3%. No further increase on PPI grounds is justified; a small downward correction is arguable.

Part 370010 (1.4404): Blankstahl's price applies the PPI-C2431 clause to a stainless part whose largest driver is the alloy surcharge (weight 0.43), not PPI-C2431. Blankstahl now pays a full +11% while the driver mix suggests about +7% over 12 months (AS +5.9% x 0.43, PPI +12.3% x 0.36, LCI). The 80% source Donautal (sup:70710) is at 5.45 (quote:7300008, material covered to March 2027), against Blankstahl's 5.84 now and its new quote of 6.06 (quote:7200008). Blankstahl is 7–11% above the rival. Donautal's 6.31 quote for a small volume of 23,700 (quote:7200018) is a small-lot price and weakens the comparison only slightly. AS-14404 is -5.5% from its 2026-06 high. The supplier's 2026-09-22 request for an AS-14404 clause would replace the PPI link with a more fitting index. Room: about 5.45–5.60.

Part 370012 (C45): Rupprecht-Kessel supplies at 126.05/100 and quoted 129.78 in 2025 (quote:7100067). Blankstahl's 143.39 is about 12% above the rival price. Even indexing the rival's price by +10% gives about 139, so there is room of roughly 4–8% on 370012.
Part 370020 (S235 sheet): Blankstahl's new quote of 96.37 (quote:7200016) is 14% above the incumbent's 84.34. Even with PPI-C241 at +6.5%, about 89–90 would be justified. The quote is uncompetitive.

Part 370011 is single-sourced with no benchmark; its price is back at the 2023 level (3.20). The index pass-through matches the clause, so the room is small: at most about 2% from the PPI fall since 2026-06.
Negotiation history shows Blankstahl settling about 2.7–2.9 points below its opening ask at renewals.

findings.text: Owner is personally involved and open: he twice offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material). This is a family-owned firm with an owner who engages directly. An open-book review is a lever. It could expose a stale cost basis, and it lets us test their claimed cost shares instead of accepting index-share claims.

Approval ladder: price changes above 2% need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Moves beyond 2% will be slow. Settling within ±2% may be decided by the KAM alone, so we should time rounds and make packages that fit under the threshold.

Red flag on deprioritisation. Their sales director has said three times (June, August, September 2026) that they are reviewing small accounts and focusing on customers with volume. Our spend of about EUR 428k is roughly 0.4% of their turnover, so we are small to them. Volume and a commitment are what they value; our forecasts are up on all parts (e.g. 370020 +19%, 370011 +15%).

Their ask on 370010: an AS-14404 alloy surcharge clause instead of a fixed price basis. The letter is a formal, impersonal proposal with no figure stated. The surcharge index is +5.9% year on year but -5.5% since June 2026, so the timing favours a clause only if the base is set at the current level.

Financially sound and stable: founded 1961, family owned, 200 staff, about EUR 98M turnover, equity ratio 39.3%, credit index 148 and unchanged, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001/14001. There is no sign of distress or cash pressure, so they can afford to walk away from a small account.

We pay reliably, on average 2.8 days late with none more than 10 days late. Shorter payment terms are less of a cash need for them than for a stressed supplier, but they remain a tradeable courtesy. The current contract term is already 30 days net against our 60-day standard.
Sales contact changed to a new inside-sales colleague in October 2025. A newer contact may defer to the KAM, the committee or the owner. The trade-fair news is noise.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070740 covers part:370010, part:370011 and part:370012. It runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice, so the notice deadline is 2026-11-01. The exit option is still open and credible for 370010 and 370012, but not for 370011, where they are our single source.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 60 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-11-01. On top of that, an index clause on PPI-C2431 applies: material share 0.8, base is the index two months before the price year, quarterly adjustment if the move exceeds 3%. PPI-C2431 rose 12.3% in 12 months, so the clause, not a negotiated ask, is the supplier's main route to an increase. Order prices already jumped mid-2026: 370011 from 2.88 to 3.20, 370012 from 129.13 to 143.39, 370010 from 5.26 to 5.84. This is consistent with quarterly index adjustments having already been triggered. We should check that these were computed correctly before granting anything more.

The supplier's letter of 2026-09-22 proposes a new price basis for 370010 with an adjustment clause on AS-14404 (alloy surcharge) instead of, or in addition to, PPI-C2431. AS-14404 is +5.9% over 12 months but -5.5% since 2026-06. Any switch of index must be traded, not conceded. The existing clause already passes through 80% of price as material, which risks double-counting.

Other contract terms: payment 30 days net, against our standard of 60, which already favours them. Delivery is DAP with 14 days' lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and EUR 150 per complaint. Actual on-time delivery is 81%, well below the 95% target, which is a contractual gap we can press. Quality is excellent at 32 ppm.

History: across 9 renewals the supplier settled on average 2.7-2.9 percentage points below its ask, often turning a requested increase into a cut. Examples: 370011 asked +1.8%, settled -1.7%; 370012 asked +3.0%, settled -0.3%. They concede readily. Note that price changes above 2% need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks, so this affects timing.

Dependency differs by part:
- 370010: they hold only a 20% share; sup:70710 holds 80% and we pay it 5.45 versus 5.84 here.
- 370012: they hold 60%; sup:70720 holds 40% at 126.05 versus 143.39.
- 370011: they are our single source at 100%, so this part is our exposure.
Tooling is listed as n/a in sourcing despite library claims that the supplier owns it; this is likely not a real switching barrier for bar stock. We are 0.4% of their turnover, and their sales director repeatedly signals a focus on volume customers.

findings.text: Delivery is the weak spot and is not improving: on-time vs requested date has held at 81-84% for two years (86.5% in 2024Q3/Q4, 81.0% rolling to 2026-09) against the contractual 95% target and a peer median of 84.6%. On-time vs its own confirmed date has slid from 93.2% (2024Q4) to 83.5%, so it is missing even its own promises more often. Late receipts average 9 days, max 28.

Lateness is concentrated on part:370011 (1.4021, single source): 22.2% late, avg 12 days, max 28 in the last 12 months. part:370010 is late often (15.4%) but only by about 4.5 days. part:370012 shows 7.7% early deliveries and 80.8% confirmed-date OTD.

Quality is a strength that argues its case: rolling ppm fell from 111 (2025Q1) to 32 (2026Q3) with 5 complaints, versus a peer median of 457 ppm. It has 0 overdue 8Ds and keeps class A green with score about 90-91. The 32 complaints over three years were recharged at the EUR 150 flat fee, with modest cost to us. The remaining issues are mostly handling and documentation: burrs, missing marking, wrong certificates.

Prices jumped mid-2026 on all three parts. part:370010 went from 5.26 to 5.84 (+11%), part:370011 from 2.88 to 3.20 (+11%) and part:370012 from 129.13 to 143.39 (+11%). Rivals moved down on the same parts: sup:70710 is at 5.45 on 370010 and sup:70720 at 126.05 on 370012. That leaves this supplier 7-14% above the parallel source.

The volume outlook is positive and the forecasts are shared with the supplier. part:370011 is forecast at 90,000 kg vs 78,400 ordered (+15%), part:370012 at 98,700 vs 90,360 group-wide, and part:370010 is about flat. This fits the sales director's stated focus on customers with volume.

Ordering friction on our side is low: there are few rush lines (6/4/3) and few changed lines. Our side therefore does not explain the delivery misses. The data does not show whether its lateness caused line stoppages, so the cost of late delivery is unquantified.

arguments.text: The Q3 2026 uplift was not a discretionary increase. It is the agreed mechanism of our framework contract. PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months, and clause 3.2 passes 80 % of that through, with a 3 % deadband protecting both sides. We applied the contract as written, and in the falling years it worked in Hollerau's favour.

Over three renewals we gave Hollerau price reductions well beyond what we asked for. On 370010 the cuts were -5.7 %, -4.5 % and -4.2 %, and 370012 also fell every year. We have shared the downside generously, so it is fair to ask for symmetry now that costs rise.

Our real cost drivers are rising. The 1.4404 alloy surcharge is up about 6 % year on year to EUR 3,008/t, basic steel is up 7.3 % since January, and labour is up 2.7 %. For stainless bar, the alloy surcharge rather than the PPI is the honest cost basis. That is why we propose an AS-14404 clause for 370010: it tracks cost both ways.
Our quality is clearly improving. Overall ppm fell from 111 to 32. On 370010 we run 43 ppm against Donautal's 75. On 370011 we run 13 ppm. Fewer defects lower Hollerau's total cost.
We are a sound family company: equity ratio 39 %, stable credit index, VDA 6.3 grade A. We are the only approved source for 370011. Stability and supply security have value.
Our owner offers an open-book walk-through of hourly rates and material. We have nothing to hide.

weak_points: 370010 at 5.84 vs Donautal 5.45, and our own Sept quote of 6.06 is above that. We already lost the 2025 benchmark.
370012 at 143.39 vs Rupprecht-Kessel 126.05, which is about 14 % higher. They could shift our 60 % quota.
PPI-C2431 is 2.3 % off its peak, and we took the full 11 % in one step.
Delivery is poor: about 81-83 % on time vs the 95 % target, and 370011 is worst at 22 % late, max 28 days.
Our sheet quote of 96.37 vs their 84.34 shows we are not competitive there.
Hollerau pays reliably, only about 3 days late, so we cannot argue payment risk.
Our 'small accounts review' remarks could backfire. Hollerau is roughly EUR 430k a year, small for us, but walking away is not really our plan.
Hollerau can still give notice on the contract until about end of October.
wants: A 24-36 month extension of the framework agreement.
Binding annual volumes, especially a larger 370012 quota (back toward 70-80 %) and a higher share of 370010.
An AS-14404 alloy surcharge clause for 370010, under which we would accept a lower base price.
Recognition of the rising 370011 forecast (90 t) as a firm call-off.
Shorter payment terms, e.g. 14 days, in exchange for a small discount.
red_lines: No price on 370011 below the indexed 3.20 unless volume is binding. It is single source and our most heavily loaded part.
No fixed price for stainless 370010 beyond 12 months without an alloy surcharge mechanism.
No retroactive reversal of the contractual Q3 index adjustment.
No moves above about 2 % without committee approval. I will not promise what I cannot sign.
No matching 370012 at 126 without a quota and volume increase.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long partnership and point to the improved quality figures. Explain the Q3 adjustment as the contract working as designed, after three years of price cuts beyond our own offers. Then propose a package: extend the framework by two years and introduce the AS-14404 clause on 370010 with a modestly lower base price. Offer a small gesture on 370012 in return for a higher quota and binding volumes. Hold 370011 at the indexed price, and offer the owner's open-book review as proof of fairness. Commit to an on-time delivery improvement plan for 370011.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the uplift followed the clause we both signed, and we have honoured it in every order since. That is exactly why the cost rise in cold-drawn bar is now fully in our prices. The same index has eased since its high, so any further increase on these grounds would count the same movement twice. We would rather use the clause as it stands for this period and talk about the new price basis on that footing.

We value those settlements, and they were reached together. They mostly followed falling material markets and the benchmark position at the time, so they were not one-sided gifts. Symmetry has also already happened: the recent index step took the bar prices above where they started. On the single-source bar, today's price stands at or above its starting level.

It would have to replace the existing producer-price link rather than sit on top of it, with the base set at today's level, which is below this year's high. Weighted by its share of cost, the surcharge rise supports a far smaller change than the step already applied. Basic steel and labour carry only a small weight in a peeled bar.

Your quality progress is real and we say so internally; it is one reason we want to keep and grow the business. It does sit alongside delivery performance that stays well short of the contractual on-time target and below peers. That gap also costs us, so quality alone does not justify a price premium.

Your stability matters to us, and that is why we want a longer, firmer relationship. Supply security on the single-source bar would carry more weight with better on-time delivery, which has been weakest exactly on that part. On the parts we also source elsewhere, security is a shared value rather than a reason for a price gap. We are a reliable payer and offer the same stability in return.

We gladly accept your owner's offer and would like to go through the calculation together. That is the fairest way to settle the price basis, especially for a new surcharge clause. Meanwhile we will base our proposals on the published drivers and the cost shares they imply.

press: Our forecasts for the coming year show rising volume on all three bars, and we would like to commit part of it to you in exchange for a competitive price basis.
The producer-price index has come off its high since the last quarterly step, and we would like the clause to reflect that at the next adjustment.
Your sheet-metal quote is some way above our current supply, so we cannot consider it in its present form.
Because volume matters to you and to us, we would like to discuss a two-year commitment with binding quantities as part of a fair overall package.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 60 days before the end of the calendar year.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement ties the price to an agreed index formula.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#3.2 (index): The price follows index PPI-C2431: P = P0 x (1 - 0.8 + 0.8 x I(m-2) / I(base)), base = the index two months before the price year starts, adjusted quarterly on the 1st of January, April, July and October if the change exceeds 3 %. The series moved +12.3% in 12 months.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement sets the payment terms.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#4.1 (payment): Payment: 30 days net. Our standard is 60 days; shorter terms are its benefit.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement sets the delivery terms and the standard lead time.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#5.1 (delivery): Delivery DAP; standard lead time 14 days from order.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement includes the quality agreement with its delivery target.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#6.1 (quality): The quality agreement applies: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement renews only unless either side gives notice.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070740#8.1 (term): Valid from 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31; extends by 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice by 2026-11-01 (still open: a credible exit).
